# Independent complete audit: local Lorentz neighborhood for arbitrary planar bodies

Source: `candidate fed8703fd24ac57f`. **PASS**, for the stated ordinary planar theorem at a fixed strict-incidence triangle, fixed source, and fixed three normals. This audit does not promote the result to a global ordinary-body inequality or to mixed-fiber compatibility.

## 1. Dependencies and normalization

The source uses three independently proved inputs: the actual triangle row inequalities, the strict first variation for every interior one-point ear at a tight triangle, and the exact support-preserving six-sector replacement. I previously proved or independently audited these inputs. The ear results include both unique and double peak sectors and their crossing seams. The replacement preserves exactly the seven raw quantities used by the row functional and also the selected actual support lines; that last property is used again for equality.

The support-function comparison `(1-epsilon/r)T subset K subset (1+epsilon/r)T` is valid because the origin is interior and `h_T>=r` on the unit circle. Its intersections with rays, sectors, and source halfspaces give the asserted area and section convergence. No unsupported general boundary-section continuity is needed.

## 2. Auxiliary vertices converge in position, not just in area

Every old ray endpoint lies in the relative interior of an old triangle edge. Normalizing each selected actual support to value one at the moving endpoint gives norm at most `2/r`. Every convergent subsequence of such forms supports the limiting triangle at that edge-interior point, whose support line is unique. This proves convergence uniformly over arbitrary choices of actual supports.

In a unique sector, the limiting wedge has `p,q<1`, `D=1-pq>0`, and vertex `E=((1-p)/D,(1-q)/D)`. The positive combination of its two inequalities with weights `(1-q)/D,(1-p)/D` has both coordinate coefficients equal to one. Its unique maximizer of `u+v` is `E`, because equality forces both inequalities to be equalities. The auxiliary coefficients are bounded by their exact positive sum. Every subsequential limit satisfies the limiting wedge constraints and attains that maximal sum, so it equals `E`. Thus the tangential coordinate is controlled; area convergence alone is not being substituted for position convergence.

In a double sector the coefficient sum tends to one, so every limiting auxiliary is on the closed bridge segment. That entire segment is a positive distance from the old vertices. These two facts establish the full replacement convergence needed later for every permitted choice, rather than just one favorable replacement.

## 3. Nearby inner triangle and exact three-ear geometry

The fixed exposing functional at each old vertex has a positive gap over both other vertices and all old bridge segments. Consequently the three unique auxiliaries are exposed vertices of the replacement, and their triangle `T_0` is inside it and converges to the original triangle. All other construction points lie near old bridge interiors. Their two edge barycentric coordinates therefore have a common positive lower bound `c`, their opposite coordinate is at least `-delta`, and their edge projection parameters stay uniformly away from zero and one.

The whole-hull lemma is correct. If two coordinates `i,j` of a convex combination were negative, the weights `a_i,a_j` of their corresponding groups would obey `c a_j<delta a_i` and `c a_i<delta a_j`. Both weights must be positive, and multiplication contradicts `delta<c`. Contributions from the third group and from triangle vertices are nonnegative and are legitimately dropped.

The halfspace truncation outside one edge of this finite hull has only the outside construction vertices and intersections of hull edges with the base line as possible vertices. The no-two-negative property places every such intersection in the base segment. Thus the closed outside portion is exactly the convex hull of that base segment and its outside vertices. The three ears are disjoint except for null boundaries, and no extra joining region is omitted.

Using `w` equal to the outward quarter-turn of the edge vector divided by its squared length gives `|det(B-A,w)|=1`. The actual ear is the subgraph of a concave polygonal roof over the unit edge interval. All its nontrivial breakpoints stay in a common `[kappa,1-kappa]`. Concavity gives `H/2<=E<=H`, and the first and last slopes give the global Lipschitz bound `H/kappa`. These estimates remove endpoint concentration uniformly.

## 4. Clipping and coarea errors, including knots

For a crossing margin `Delta(s-s_0)+b h`, the actual and ideal cap indicators differ only in a strip of width at most `C H`; its height is at most `H`, giving the stated `O(H^2)` area error. No derivative of the roof is used in this estimate.

On the cutting line, the endpoint equation is `h_*=h_e(s_0-(b/Delta)h_*)`. The roof Lipschitz bound makes the right side minus `h_*` strictly decreasing when `H` is small, even at knots. Its endpoint signs provide existence, and its solution is unique. The same Lipschitz estimate yields `|h_*-h_e(s_0)|<=C H^2`.

The coarea increment really is `h_*/|Delta|`: in the determinant-one edge coordinates, integrating the affine delta function first in `s` gives precisely `dh/|Delta|`. Therefore the normalization by the original normal length is already accounted for. The two endpoint increments of each original chord are disjoint. The third vertex's cap is uniformly negative on a sufficiently small ear and has zero increment.

Summing over the three ears gives the actual data expansion with `||R||<=C delta_0 E`, because `H_e^2<=2 delta_0 E_e`. The linear increments, including section values, are bounded by `C E`. This is the required relative estimate; it remains valid when one ear is much smaller than another.

## 5. Uniform strict first variation and Taylor remainder

The row functional is `C^2` on a fixed compact positive-data neighborhood. Its quadratic Taylor remainder is `O(E^2)=O(delta_0 E)` because `E<=3 delta_0`. The constants are uniform over the nearby triangle and the fixed compact peak interval.

The positive tent decomposition is exact: the coefficient at a roof knot is `t(1-t)` times its downward slope jump. The resulting sum has the same derivative jumps and zero endpoint values as the roof. Its coefficients sum to twice the roof area. The linear data functional for a tent is the actual first derivative of an outward triangular ear with that peak; its positive normalization does not change the strict sign in the audited one-ear results.

All three edges and all peak parameters now range over a compact set separated from edge endpoints. Continuity, including crossing seams, supplies a uniform strictly negative derivative. Integrating that derivative by the positive tent decomposition gives `-2c_0 E`; the uniformly smaller `C delta_0 E` error leaves a strict negative multiple of actual total ear area. This is a justified finite neighborhood argument, not an inference from unrelated pointwise derivatives.

## 6. Equality and return to the original body

If the total ear area is positive, each initially tight row becomes strict. If it is zero, the replacement is the nearby inner triangle. Its retained ray endpoints lie in edge interiors, so every retained actual support line must be the corresponding triangle edge line. The original body lies in those three halfplanes and has the same area as the triangle. A proper closed convex subset would miss a positive-area cap by strict separation, so the original body is that triangle. Therefore a nontriangular original body cannot hide behind a triangular replacement.

Initially strict rows remain strict by the already established raw-data continuity. Intersecting the finitely many neighborhoods proves all three conclusions simultaneously. Degenerating triangles and source cuts approaching vertices are expressly outside any claimed uniform neighborhood.

No mathematical correction was required. A minor coordinate-wording clarification was suggested to make the quarter-turn definition of `w` explicit; it does not change the proof.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
